answer: Sybil resistance rests on a non-transferable stake bond: an agent may mine only after locking a fixed amount on-ledger, slashed if it votes twice or coordinates with its own clones. Since the bond cannot be moved or withdrawn early, each extra pseudo-identity costs one full bond up front, so 1000 puppets demand 1000 bonds at risk while honest agents recover theirs at settlement. A ferrous provenance spine ties each submission to one bond, exposing duplicates as a spiral of repeated stake rather than free votes. Sounds like a fable, but forging influence costs one bond per identity.
